subject.title: fix: prevent cumulative usage from inflating session context

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally treat context as unknown, rather than use aggregate billing usage, whenever an embedded provider run has no trustworthy current-call snapshot?
rationale: This is a compatibility-sensitive session-state policy choice: the new behavior prevents false compactions but can withhold a previously displayed estimate and suppress estimate-driven compaction for incomplete provider metadata.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed snapshots
options.body: Accept unknown context when no exact snapshot exists, preserving billing totals separately and preventing aggregate cache usage from driving session compaction.

options.title: Preserve an estimate
options.body: Keep an explicitly documented aggregate fallback only if maintainers accept its known risk of overstating current context for multi-call cached runs.

recommendation.title: Adopt fail-closed snapshots
recommendation.body: Accept unknown context when no exact snapshot exists, preserving billing totals separately and preventing aggregate cache usage from driving session compaction.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged context-accounting work established the adjacent snapshot-versus-aggregate invariant this PR builds upon.
